Subject: Follow-up — packaging and channel passback details

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo today — the team liked the latency profile and the dedicated capacity guarantee. Procurement asked me to collect a bit more detail before we move to the PO stage: specifically we need a line-item view showing the proposed SKU repackaging for marketplace/private-offer, the list price vs net after discounts, and the expected channel passback / reseller margin.

Can you provide:
- a simple Excel with SKU mappings and per-SKU list vs final price
- a margin workback that shows Redwood net rev after reseller fee and any marketplace take
- any evidence (previous invoice or signed MAP) that demonstrates how passback has been handled for similar customers

We are aiming to lock terms this week if possible. Attaching our procurement template for your convenience.

Thanks,
Aditi
Procurement Lead, NovaWorks

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up — packaging and channel passback details

Hi Aditi — great to meet you virtually this morning.

Short answer: yes. I've attached two files that should cover what procurement requested: SKU_packaging_v2.xlsx (line-item mapping + list vs proposed private-offer net price) and channel_margin_workback.pdf (per-sku calculations showing reseller fee, marketplace fee, and final Redwood net). I also included a redacted MAP previously signed with a reseller to show real-world invoicing flow (signed-MAP-redlines.pdf).

Notes/high-level:
- We propose repackaging the offer into three marketplace SKUs (Base, Scale, Enterprise) to simplify invoicing and reduce metering complexity for NovaWorks.
- Two channel margin options are included in the workback: (A) flat reseller fee (8% on gross) and (B) tiered passback (10% up to $100k / 6% thereafter). In both options the marketplace listing fee is modeled separately and passed through.
- The attached workback includes a model showing how each option impacts Redwood net ARR at multiple usage tiers.

Ask from you: please confirm whether NovaWorks needs reseller invoices routed via a distributor (we'll need partner billing evidence) or if direct reseller passback is acceptable. Also confirm whether the buyer requires a first-year usage commitment for the early-adopter discount.

I'll loop in Ben to confirm comp and legal checks below.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL — pricing posture and recommended channel structure for NovaWorks

Team — quick internal note so we have a unified response to procurement.

Summary of ask: NovaWorks wants SKU-level transparency and a clear passback calculation they can share with their finance team. They also want evidence of prior invoices / MAP.

Recommendation (two tracks):
1) Conservative (preserve net): Flat reseller fee of 8% on gross list for the private-offer SKUs. This is easiest for NovaWorks and keeps our GAAP reconciliation simple.
2) Incentivized (growth tilt): Tiered passback: 10% reseller fee up to $100k/month, then 6% on incremental consumption. Offer a 5% early-adopter discount applied to Redwood net for the first 12 months if they commit to a 12-month minimum.

Action items:
- Soojin to propose both options to procurement and ask whether they require distributor pass-through evidence (if so, Connor to prepare partner invoice redaction).
- Irene to confirm legal on whether the early-adopter discount triggers any marketplace listing repricing constraints.
- Ben to sign off on the proposed 5% first-year discount cap.

I've added a quick working tab in the attached workbook that shows net revenue under both options across three usage scenarios. Will update with partner invoice evidence if procurement needs it.

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
attachment: internal_SKU_working_tab.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novaworks.ai>

Thanks Soojin — we received the files and procurement is reviewing. A few clarifying requests from our finance team: 

1) They want a single line-item export showing for each SKU: list price, private-offer price, reseller fee amount, marketplace fee amount, and Redwood net. The workbook has this but can you provide a CSV export we can ingest?
2) We need one example (anonymized) invoice showing how passback was handled operationally for a prior reseller scenario — the signed MAP is helpful but finance needs an invoice-level example. If you can provide a partner invoice redaction that shows the passback line, that would accelerate approvals.
3) Budget team asks whether the early-adopter 5% is stackable with any marketplace coupon/intro credit or if that would double-count. Please clarify how discounts are applied.

Also, procurement would prefer the tiered passback structure if Redwood can commit to the first-year discount and provide the invoice redaction. Otherwise we'll ask for the flat fee option in our approval memo.

Appreciate quick turnaround — we are targeting a PO by Friday.

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
Sr. Procurement Manager, NovaWorks

Marta / Aditi — thanks for the clear asks. Attached are: the requested CSV export (SKU_packaging_v2.csv exported from the workbook), a partner invoice redaction (partner_invoice_redacted.pdf) that shows passback line items, and a short writeup that clarifies discount stacking rules (discount_stack_note.pdf).

Quick answers:
- Invoice export: see SKU_packaging_v2.csv, columns: SKU_ID, SKU_Name, List_Price, Private_Offer_Price, Reseller_Fee, Marketplace_Fee, Redwood_Net.
- Partner invoice evidence: partner_invoice_redacted.pdf demonstrates reseller passback where the reseller fee is credited to the partner and the buyer is invoiced the private-offer net. We redacted partner names and amounts where required.
- Discount stacking: Redwood applies discounts sequentially to the Redwood list price for the private offer. Marketplace coupons apply on the final list price before Redwood passback calculations; the early-adopter 5% is applied to Redwood net (after marketplace fees) and is not stackable with marketplace coupons that explicitly say they cannot be combined. The attached note explains the precedence and examples.

Proposed commercial stance: we recommend the tiered passback (Option B) with the 5% first-year early-adopter discount; this preserves NovaWorks' target economics while leaving room for growth. If you sign the PO with the tiered passback and commit to 12 months, we will lock the discount.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which passback option you prefer and whether you require distributor routing evidence (if so, we will provide the distributor invoice redaction).
2) If accepted, we'll prepare a DocuSign PO and the private-offer package for your legal team.

Link to the HubSpot deal for convenience: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
